title: Built-in milling vises: parametric generic vises (3-8 in and 100-200 mm jaw widths) in the fixture library, jaw opening set from the stock

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Requested by the reporter of #339 (2026-11-11): CamCraft should come with **stock vises** ready to place, not only imported ones.

**What:** a set of generic, parametric milling-machine vises in the fixture library:
- **Imperial:** jaw width **3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 in**.
- **Metric:** the common 100 / 125 / 150 / 160 / 200 mm sizes.

Each is a simple solid model, original geometry built from a few parameters, not any vendor's model:
- jaw width and jaw height;
- maximum opening;
- overall length, width and base height;
- fixed jaw, moving jaw, and a screw and handle housing kept as a conservative block.

**Behaviour:**
- **Place it** into a setup like any fixture (the #339 slice-6 library), as one undoable command.
- **Jaw opening is a parameter.** It can be set to the stock's width so the moving jaw sits against the part, and the collision checks see the real jaw positions.
- **Collision checks** judge it by its mesh, like any meshed fixture (#339 slice 1).
- **A size table,** researched from public catalog spec sheets: jaw width, jaw height, max opening and overall length per size, as typical values. It's recorded in the decision file. Users can edit the dimensions to match their own vise.

Starting figures from a first search (to be confirmed in the work):
- 3 in: ~1 5/16 in high, ~4 3/4-5 in opening.
- 4 in: ~1 1/4 in high, ~6 in opening.
- 6 in: ~1 3/4 in high, ~5.5-9 in opening.
- 8 in: ~2 in high, ~8.25 in opening.

Effort: high (fixture geometry feeds the collision checks).

**Done means:**
- Every listed size can be placed from the library, with an adjustable jaw opening.
- The mesh is checked by the fixture laws.
- Pinned by tests: a placed 6 in vise collides with a tool path that crosses its jaw, and doesn't collide with one that clears it.
- Undo removes it.

Part of #339.
